pending_commit.commit_message: battery: Allow BATTERY_LEVEL_NEAR_FULL to be defined by board Allow the board to override the hardcoded 97% value for reporting to the host (and controlling LED behavior) when the battery is "near full". When enabling "discharge on ac" with a full battery the battery stops taking a charge until it reaches ~94% SOC (the actual value is not set but rather comes from a smart battery status bit) but the user will see the device as discharging between 97% and 94%. The host side view can be worked around with a powerd preference. The LED behavior is all inside the EC, so you end up with the LED showing discharging when it should not. If we allow the board to override this to 94% then the LED and host behavior is consistent. BUG=b:36024657 BRANCH=none TEST=make -j buildall Change-Id: Ie5ab8e41b87101e201073276bf441e25be7daca4 Signed-off-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/450949 Reviewed-by: Scott Collyer <scollyer@chromium.org>

g: mark RW INFO rollback map space to match the header infomap field The cr50 RO image compares INFO rollback map space against the contents of the RW image's infomap field. To ensure that no rollback is possible, the RW should verify that the INFO space state is consistent with the current RW and RW_B headers, and if not, update the INFO state to comply. This should happen only when running prod images, so that debug images could be rolled back if so desired. Also fixed the bug in functions enabling read and write access to the INFO1 region. Write access is now a superset of read access setting. auto_updater: reduce devserver cpu load using scp. We switch from rsync to scp to copy autoupdate artifacts. Notice the latter are already compressed, and old artifacts are cleaned up before calling rsync. rsync should only be used for delta compression, e.g. when the destination file(s) exist and are mostly identical. Even then it should not be used for already compressed files with --compress, which remote_access.py Rsync does by default (good for copying log files, bad for copying already compressed binaries). Anyhow, three experiments: Notice below in 1) that for rsync --compress one CPU is pegged and transfer is limited by CPU at 21MB/s. Notice that in 2) rsync (no --compress) that transfer is currently not limited by CPU but limited by DUT USB 2.0 dongle at 33MB/s. CPU might get limited at about 100MB/s, or if hit DUTs with USB 3.0 dongles. Notice that in 3) scp the transfer is about the same as in 2) at 34MB/s. But CPU overhead drops further. 1) rsync with compression (and block hashing, but destination empty) chromeos-test@chromeos4-devserver3:~/images$ time rsync --perms --verbose --times --compress --omit-dir-times --exclude .svn --links /home/chromeos-test/images/gandof-release/R59-9344.0.0/update.gz root@chromeos4-row5-rack8-host3:/mnt/stateful_partition/unencrypted/preserve/cros-update/ sent 1,002,139,079 bytes received 35 bytes 21,551,378.80 bytes/sec total size is 1,002,795,430 speedup is 1.00 real 0m46.546s user 0m46.464s sys 0m2.020s 2) rsync without compression (still block hashing, destination empty) chromeos-test@chromeos4-devserver3:~/images$ time rsync --perms --verbose --times --omit-dir-times --exclude .svn --links /home/chromeos-test/images/gandof-release/R59-9344.0.0/update.gz root@chromeos4-row5-rack8-host3:/mnt/stateful_partition/unencrypted/preserve/cros-update/ sent 1,003,040,329 bytes received 35 bytes 32,886,569.31 bytes/sec total size is 1,002,795,430 speedup is 1.00 real 0m30.166s user 0m11.428s sys 0m2.672s 3) scp (no compression, no block hashing) chromeos-test@chromeos4-devserver3:~/images$ time scp /home/chromeos-test/images/gandof-release/R59-9344.0.0/update.gz root@chromeos4-row5-rack8-host3:/mnt/stateful_partition/unencrypted/preserve/cros-update/ 100% 956MB 34.2MB/s 00:28 real 0m29.348s user 0m5.740s sys 0m3.420s Example of current use: chromeo+ 31387 24508 68 20:53 ? check_ethernet.hook: Fix the ambiguious matching of ssh connections As the ARC++ is introduced on Chromebook, the sshd port 22 is also used for adb connection for simplicity and the real sshd is then running on port 2222 instead. However, this also introduces a bug in check_ethernet.hook to include the 127.0.0.1 in the results of listing ssh connections. The patch addresses this issue by fixing the regular expression to retrieve the ssh connections only. BUG=chromium:695366 TEST=only DUT in lab === original regular expression on DUT ==== localhost ~ # find_ssh_client() { netstat -lanp | awk '/tcp.*:22.*ESTABLISHED.*/ {split($5,a,":"); print a[1]}'; } localhost ~ # find_ssh_client 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1 127.0.0.1 172.25.75.19 172.30.210.13 172.25.75.19 === with the fix === find_ssh_client() { > netstat -lanp | awk '/tcp.*:22 .*ESTABLISHED.*/ {split($5,a,":"); print a[1]}' > } localhost ~ # find_ssh_client 172.25.75.19 172.30.210.13 172.25.75.19 Change-Id: If3163ab80a06e0e6b5596fe1ae8454504be8cfd2 Signed-off-by: Chung-yih Wang <cywang@google.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/452057 Reviewed-by: Richard Barnette <jrbarnette@google.com>

By default it won't exit on the first usb failure it will run through all of the iterations. There are a couple of Cr50 issues with USB and we want to see if we are making improvements in the percent of usb interactions that failed.
